title: Jev CEO: I made ChatGPT, now I'm building what's next
talk_summary: A former OpenAI post-training researcher argues that RLHF-trained models are optimized for human preference (assistance), which makes them sycophantic and unreliable for autonomous automation, and pitches a stealth startup building a post-training stack optimized for calibrated decision-making. The talk is mostly conceptual/positioning with no concrete engineering techniques, benchmarks, or reproducible mechanisms.

takeaways.technique: Calibration over preference in reviewer prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues RLHF models are trained to look right rather than be right, so they overclaim confidence; automation needs calibrated, correctness-first outputs instead of pleasing the human.
takeaways.evidence_quote: no matter how wrong the models are, they will look right because of the asymmetry within the reward model

takeaways.technique: Separate assistance vs automation success criteria
takeaways.what_they_do: Distinguishes tasks whose goal is pleasing a human-in-the-loop from tasks that must run unattended correctly; says the two need different optimization targets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the goal of it is to please the human in the loop ... on the other side ... the goal is to not have remove the human loop

takeaways.technique: Don't let agents make high-stakes irreversible decisions
takeaways.what_they_do: Observes businesses keep AI away from decisions with real stakes, pushing cost/risk to the user rather than the business.
takeaways.evidence_quote: do not use AI for decisions with stakes to your business
